routes.label: Model the points with one unknown

question: The players on a basketball team made some three-point shots, some two-point shots, and some one-point free throws. They scored as many points with two-point shots as with three-point shots. Their number of successful free throws was one more than their number of successful two-point shots. The team’s total score was \(61\) points. How many free throws did they make?
solution:
Use the number of two-point shots to express all three contributions to the score. Let \(t\) be the number of successful two-point shots. Those shots contributed \(2t\) points, and the three-point shots contributed the same \(2t\) points. The team made \(t+1\) free throws, contributing \(t+1\) points.

Adding the three contributions gives
\[
2t+2t+(t+1)=61,
\]
so \(5t+1=61\), and hence \(t=12\). The number of free throws was therefore \(12+1=13\).

These counts satisfy all the conditions: \(12\) two-point shots and \(8\) three-point shots each contribute \(24\) points, and \(24+24+13=61\). The answer is \(\boxed{13}\), choice A.
